inputs.text: South Portland’s school shortfall is being made to land on students and the workers who teach and support them, with more than 70 positions set to be cut. That is not an abstract budget exercise: it risks weakening basic education and deepening the strain on families and school staff. The district needs to explain openly how it reached this point and what priorities put these jobs at risk. Accountability should mean scrutinizing those choices—not treating cuts to classrooms and workers as the only path to “discipline.”
